new.n: Pedlar McArdill's robbery gold, dry well in the Newbre neighbourhood, Emmett Twp (1844 robbery; 1874 dig)
new.pl: N. A. Burton's 160 acres, sec. 27 T2S R7W, Emmett Twp (1873 Calhoun directory), south of the Kalamazoo River; well not yet placed on a plat
new.st: About 1844 John McArdill, a jewellery pedlar from London, Canada, was robbed of $4,000-5,000. In 1873 an anonymous letter from a former farmhand said he and a partner had hidden the loot in a 40-ft dry well in the Newbre neighbourhood south of the Kalamazoo River, filled in with earth, stones and oak stumps. The well was found on N. A. Burton's lot exactly as described. In Sep 1874 McArdill's party pulled the stumps and dug to 50 ft, reporting nothing. By late October 'the belief has become almost universal' that McArdill got the money on the last day: a neighbour said the diggers had not reached bottom when he went to dinner and were hastily filling the hole when he came back. Pin is the Burton quarter-section, not the well.
new.t: Two independent 1874 papers; a recovery was rumoured but never admitted. The letter put the well under half a mile N of the gravel road and about 8 paces from a N-S road, which the 1873 plat roads should fix. Private farmland: ask permission.
src: Calhoun County directory (1873), Emmett Twp, pp. 225-228 (HathiTrust mdp.39015071405677): N. A. Burton, 160 acres, sec. 27
pinev: Burton's 160 acres in sec. 27 T2S R7W per the 1873 directory (Newbre farms in secs 32, 34, 35 to the S); sec. 27 box 42.2613-42.2759 N, -85.1204 to -85.1006 W; on dry land (USGS 3DEP). Refine from the 1873 plate roads.
new.tovw: Lead grade C (treasure thread): two independent 1874 papers

new.n: Israel McConnell's buried gold, Okauchee House stage inn
new.pl: Okauchee House (built 1841) on the old plank road (later US 16) at Okauchee, Oconomowoc Twp
new.st: Whelan's 1949 Wisconsin Magazine of History article on the Okauchee House tells of the buried gold of Israel McConnell (b. 1795 Vermont, d. 10 May 1871), who kept the stage house until his death; someone later dug a pick hole for it. Pin is the inn at Okauchee, not a spot. Not the Crazy Man's Island story on the lake.
new.t: Legend from a 1949 article with no period record yet; the full article is waiting on JSTOR. Private property: look only.
src: Wisconsin Magazine of History 33:1 (Sep 1949), Whelan, 'The Okauchee House'
US census 1870, Oconomowoc Twp: Israel McConnell, hotel keeper
pinev: Okauchee House per HABS WIS-11 on the old plank road; lot not confirmed on a plat. Pin at GNIS Okauchee (on land, USGS 3DEP).
new.tovw: Lead grade D (treasure thread): 1949 secondary telling only

tw-ia-north-mcgregor-taylor-gold.st: The 1906 syndicate feature printed the note as 'ON HIGHEST BLUFF ACROSS FROM FORT IN 4 PILES EACH 20,000 PIERRE MERCIERRE' and put Fort McKay 'near where the little town of North McGregor, Iowa, now stands'. In Feb 1905 hundreds were digging on the bluff, and Taylor's parties dug for days in 1906; 'never a trace was found'.
tw-ia-north-mcgregor-taylor-gold.t: No recovery was reported 1905-10, and the bluff has been dug over.
src: Inter Ocean (Chicago), 28 Oct 1906, p. 38, 'Iowans Locate Black Hawk's Treasure' (Newspapers.com 34545484)
